name: Alpenblumengarten Kitzbüheler Horn
kurzbeschreibung: The Alpenblumengarten am Kitzbüheler Horn at 1,880 m: over 400 rare high-alpine plants from around the world across 20,000 m² of panoramic grounds.
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous Alpenblumengarten am Kitzbüheler Horn is situated at an altitude of 1,880 metres directly below the distinctive peak of the Kitzbüheler Horn in the Kitzbüheler Alpen. Covering more than 20,000 square metres on a sun-drenched high plateau, this botanical show garden ranks among the most species-rich and beautiful high-mountain gardens in all of Europe. Featuring over 400 rare, protected plant species from the Alps, the Caucasus, the Andes, the Himalayas, and the Pyrenees, the site combines cutting-edge botanical research with a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic view of the rugged limestone cliffs of the Wilder Kaiser, the Loferer Steinberge, and the snow-capped Hohe Tauern.

Botanical Diversity & Alpine Garden

The show garden was established in 1985 through the initiative of the Kitzbüheler Bergbahnen and dedicated botanists from the Universität Innsbruck. The grounds were designed so that plants thrive in near-natural recreated biotopes—from calcareous rock crevices and primary rock screes to acidic dwarf-shrub heaths, snow beds, and raised bogs. Strolling along the well-maintained serpentine paths, visitors discover botanical treasures such as genuine Edelweiss (Leontopodium nivale), Blue Gentian, rare auricula, bellflowers, arnica, alpine roses, and exotic high-mountain flora from distant continents. Informative display panels explain the remarkable survival strategies of alpine flora against extreme cold, ultraviolet radiation, and brief growing seasons. At the heart of the garden lies an idyllic artificial alpine pond with rare aquatic and riparian vegetation. During the peak flowering season from June to August, the steep mountain plateau transforms into a vibrant sea of colours.

Visit & Getting There

The Alpenblumengarten is open daily during the summer season of the Bergbahn Kitzbühel from late May to early November, from 08:30 to 17:00. Admission to the Alpenblumengarten is free—visitors only require a mountain railway ticket or can use the toll-paying panoramic road. Hornbahn fares (2025/2026 season): round trip to the summit station adults approx. €35.00, youth approx. €26.00, children (born 2009–2018) approx. €17.50; toddlers travel free. Holders of the Kitzbüheler Alpen Sommer Card use the cable car free of charge. Travel by cable car: the 6-seater gondola lift Hornbahn departs directly from Kitzbühel and takes visitors across two sections to the middle station or the summit (followed by a short walk downhill to the garden). Alternatively, drive up the toll-paying Panoramastraße Kitzbüheler Horn to the Alpenhaus at 1,670 m. By public transport: ÖBB train to Kitzbühel station, then approximately a 10-minute walk to the valley station of the Hornbahn.

Tips

The main paths through the show garden are firmly paved and secured with handrails; however, sturdy hiking shoes are recommended due to the alpine slope and individual terrain steps. Twice daily in July and August, experienced alpine botanists offer free guided tours through the botanical garden. Stop by the adjacent Alpenhaus or the Gipfelhaus to enjoy traditional Tyrolean Kaiserschmarrn on the panoramic sun terrace.
